reasoning: Recent Montana U.S. Senate general‑election polling in the last 45 days consistently shows Republican Kurt Alme leading any multi‑candidate or two‑way configuration, with margins generally in the mid‑single to low‑double digits in three‑way trials and mid‑single digits in the closest two‑way trial. Three‑way ballots with Alme, Democrat Alani Bankhead, and independent Seth Bodnar typically have Alme around the mid‑40s to just under 50 with a lead of roughly 10–20 points over the nearest opponent, while the most competitive head‑to‑head poll shows Bodnar leading Alme by 6, and other head‑to‑heads show Alme ahead of both Bodnar and Bankhead by 3–15 points. Taken together, the recent polling implies that as of mid‑August 2026 the Senate race environment in Montana is structurally R+ high single to low double digits, with some volatility depending on whether the general election ultimately features a two‑way or three‑way ballot; there is no fresh, state‑specific Montana presidential general‑election polling in the last 45 days from qualifying outlets, so only the Senate margin can be assessed from current data.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice / Bullfinch Group summary
sources.details: Bullfinch Group statewide likely-voter poll for Independent Center/Independent Leadership Council finds Alme leading a full-field Senate ballot 36% to Bodnar 24% and Bankhead 22%, a 12-point lead over the nearest opponent.

sources.name: New York Times polls tracker (Bullfinch Group entry)
sources.details: New York Times Montana U.S. Senate polling roundup lists Bullfinch Group poll sponsored by Independent Center/Independent Leadership Council showing Alme +12 in a three-way ballot among likely voters.

sources.name: New York Times polls tracker (Hart Research entry)
sources.details: Same New York Times tracker cites a Hart Research Associates poll for The Majority Institute finding Alme leading the Senate race by 6 points in a tested configuration.

sources.name: New York Times polls tracker (GQR/Contours entries)
sources.details: New York Times tracker reports multiple GQR surveys for Contours Inc. showing Alme ahead by margins ranging from 4 to 14 points in varying ballot tests including three-way and head-to-heads, with Bodnar occasionally leading Bankhead.

sources.name: GQR poll via Strength In Numbers
sources.details: G. Elliott Morris (Strength In Numbers) publishes GQR poll showing in a hypothetical two-way Senate race Bodnar would lead Alme 50–44, while Bankhead would trail Alme 44–52.

sources.name: Tavern Research "The Tavern Take" Montana Senate poll
sources.details: Tavern Research likely-voter Montana Senate poll finds in a full field Alme at 49%, Bodnar 27%, Bankhead 24% (22-point lead over Bodnar), and in head-to-heads a 51–49 contest vs. Bodnar and 59–41 vs. Bankhead.

sources.name: The Hill summary of Strength In Numbers poll
sources.details: The Hill article on Montana Senate dynamics summarizes a Strength In Numbers July poll as finding Bodnar would beat Alme 50–44 in a two-way, while Alme would beat Bankhead 52–44.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice analytical article on Bullfinch poll
sources.details: Independent Center Voice writeup of statewide survey reiterates Bullfinch Group finding that Alme leads an open three-way U.S. Senate race 36–24–22 among likely voters, emphasizing his double-digit advantage.

sources.name: Washington Reporter summary of NRSC internal poll
sources.details: Washington Reporter reports NRSC internal polling showing Alme at 45%, Bankhead 30%, Bodnar 15% in a three-way, plus head-to-heads with Alme leading Bodnar 50–43 and Bankhead 49–46.

sources.name: Montana Free Press coverage of GOP polling
sources.details: Montana Free Press article on dropout pressure cites GOP-aligned polling with a three-way ballot showing Alme at 45%, Bankhead 30%, Bodnar 15%, implying a 15-point lead for Alme.

sources.name: Flathead Beacon synthesis of multiple Montana Senate polls
sources.details: Flathead Beacon overview notes that various polls show Bodnar and Bankhead together splitting roughly 45–49% of the vote while Alme hovers just above 40%, suggesting a Republican lead in most tested scenarios.

sources.name: NBC News Montana Senate primary results
sources.details: NBC News reports Montana’s 2026 Senate primary results, showing Alme and Bankhead winning their respective primaries decisively; this confirms nominees but does not itself provide a general-election margin.

sources.name: PredictionHunt coverage of Montana Senate betting odds
sources.details: PredictionHunt analysis of Kalshi and PredictIt markets notes GOP implied odds for winning the Montana Senate seat moving from 90% down to 80% and then back up to 88%, reflecting market expectations rather than direct vote margins.
